I went to the doctor yesterday for my annual physical and he said everything looked fine except for my weight. We talked about dieting and fitness and he gave me some very solid advice I thought I would share with you guys because you might find it helpful.

First don't over do it. Take everything nice and slow at first so I don't hurt myself.

Second, don't start a diet right off the bat. Get into the habit of walking first. He told me I am obviously going to not like walking everyday since it leaves my legs sore and I am really not going to like dieting. To avoid being discouraged by the double hate, I should focus on one thing before incorporating the other into my routine.

Third, once I have the diet and daily walking routine down pat, stick to it but don't over do it.

I went walking around 2am and I forgot to set the app I use to track distance. But I took the same route I took Monday, so it should be around an equal distance. I ain't too worried about distance right now though, just want to get into the habit of walking daily (or nightly).

It brings tears to my eyes, it really does, to read this. One year from now you'll be in the best shape you can recall. Two years? Perhaps the best shape you've ever been in. Time is on your side. It's working with you instead of against you.

Edit: On the diet: Focus on eating only healthy foods and don't be afraid to pig out on nutrition. I went through this before--my body was used to having mostly carbs so switching food types literally required a change of my internal chemistry. Let your body adapt.

Don't worry about counting calories/carbs/fats/protein for the first month but I will give you inight on what to do when you get there now.

After you are in the habit of buying and eating the good stuff, baseline your calorie intake over the span of a week. Say it's an average of 3500 calories a day. When you're ready to cut calories, cut just 100 calories every week--and try to do something like 50% carbs, 30% protein, and 20% fat (you can research this yourself, basically, the best way to calculate it is to do the equation that follows)

protein (grams) = (0.7 gram protein/1 lb) * bodyweight (lbs)

So if you weigh 300 lbs, you should try to get 210 grams of protein in your daily calorie intake. Ratchet this down as your weight drops. The fats just kind of happen when you consume good protein sources like pork chops or olive oil glazed and broiled / baked chicken, they're fine. It's the sugary carbs that are the enemy.

When you make your first cut, you'll be happy to know that you won't even notice that you're down to 3400 calories a day. In fact, you won't start to get hungry until you're below 2000 calories a day. You don't have to rush it. Stick to that -100 from baseline for maybe a couple weeks--as long as you're losing 1 pound a week, you're moving at a good pace. 1 pound per week should be your goal once you're in a routine and ready to cut.
